List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy

Impact of English on medium culture
†*281.SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the education being imparted in English
medium in schools is spoiling the life style,
language, customs and traditions of people
of various communities;
(b) if so, the efforts being made to check
the same; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Amount deposited in National
Investment Fund
*282. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are parking the
money in the National Investment Fund
(NIF);
(b) if so, the details of such money
parked in NIF during the last two years,
year-wise;
(c) whether Government are taking up
any developmental projects with the
money;
(d) if so, the details of such activities
undertaken during the last two years; and
(e) the present status of NIF?
Completion of Tillari Irrigation
Project
*283. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Tillari Irrigation Project
in Maharashtra has been completed;
(b) if so, the land proposed to be
irrigated under the project;
(c) the land presently brought under
cultivation, both in Goa and Maharashtra;
(d) whether the displaced persons have
been rehabilitated; and
(e) if so, the details of the scheme for
their rehabilitation?

89
Tenure based appointments in ONGC
*284. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether field operators in drilling
and work over rigs are being appointed on
tenure basis in Western Region in ONGC;
(b) whether there is any provision of
tenure basis engagement in the recruitment
policy of ONGC;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the policy of tenure basis
engagement has been accepted by the
concerned unions/associations;
(e) whether the present tenure based
appointments against regular posts are as
per requirement; and
(f) the terms and conditions of tenure
basis appointees?
Emergency landing of AI aircrafts
*285. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during the
last ten months, four Air India aircrafts
suffered damage like tyre burst,
malfunctioning of weather radar or aircraft
engine, which forced the pilots to make
emergency landings in Mumbai-Delhi, thus
causing unnecessary tension amongst
passengers and Air India suffering a huge
financial loss thereby;
(b) if so, the reasons for malfunctioning
of weather radar, engines, etc. since rigid
pre-takeoff tests are always enforced;
and
(c) what steps have been taken to ensure
that such situations do not recur?
New open sky regime
*286. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether pushing ahead with PM's
offer for an open sky in SAARC region,
India has sent out detailed letters outlining
the offer to all SAARC members except
Pakistan and has even extended fifty
freedom rights for flights operating within
the region;
(b) whether his Ministry has expressed
reservations about joining the open sky
agreement of ASEAN by 2010 and wants
to join regime only after 2012;
(c) whether most of the ASEAN
countries plan to follow an open sky regime
from 2010 and have invited India to be part
of the planned liberalisation;
(d) if so, the main reasons for the same;
and
(e) whether any agreement in this regard
has been reached?
Filling up of vacancies in IA in
Chennai
*287. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the number of vacant posts in
Southern Regional Establishment of Indian
Airlines in Chennai, post-wise;
(b) by when, these vacancies will be
filled up; and
(c) whether casual labours are being
engaged against the vacancies?

90
Opening of new agriculture accounts
*288. SHRI SUDARSHAN
AKARAPU: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of new agriculture
accounts opened by banks during the last
three years, year-wise;
(b) what are the targets set for opening
new agriculture accounts during the current
financial year (2006-07) and the
achievements made there against as on
31st October, 2006; and
(c) the total amount of agriculture credit
disbursed by banks during the last three
years vis-a-vis the targets set by
Government/RBI?
Supply of gas to RGTPP
*289. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) how much quantity of gas is presently
available at Ramgarh Gas Thermal Power
Project (RGTPP);
(b) the quantum of additional quantity of
gas which would  still be required to run
the plant at full capacity;
(c) the name of the agency who would
supply additional gas for this project; and
(d) by when, gas will be made available
to run both the Gas Turbines at full load?
Additional morning flight to Ranchi
from Delhi
*290. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) by when, Ranchi will be connected to
Delhi by an additional morning flight; and
(b) whether there is any plan with Indian
Airlines to have a direct flight from Ranchi
to Mumbai?
Mortgaging of tractors for taking
tractor loan
†*291. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the farmers of Mahoba District of Uttar
Pradesh have bought tractors by taking loans
from banks for which they mortgaged their
tractors and their land;
(b) the number of tractors for which
farmers took loans from the year 2002, till
date;
(c) whether Government are aware that
due to inadequate rainfall these farmers
could not deposit the instalments of tractors
and now their land is being auctioned and
tractors of many farmers have been seized;
and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to save farmers from this complex situation?
Complaints of fraud in IFCI
†*292. SHRI MAHENDRA SAHNI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any complaint regarding fraud in Industrial
Finance Corporation of India (IFCI);
(b) if so, the details of the complaint; and
(c) by when, the findings of this probe
is likely to be received?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

91
Loans to risky areas by banks
†*293. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that public
sector banks of the country have given
more loans to risky areas during the year,
2005-06 as compared to the previous
year;
(b) if so, to what extent its percentage is
more and whether such risky areas have
been identified;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the percentage of loan out of the total
loans given to each sector by these public
sector banks during the said year?
Withdrawal of guarantee cover on LIC
policies
†*294. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
withdrawing its guarantee cover on policies
of Life Insurance Corporation of India;
(b) if not, whether Government are
contemplating on withdrawing its guarantee
cover on new policies;
(c) if so, whether transaction of LIC
would not get affected in view of decrease
in number of policy holders; and
(d) if so, the details of steps to be taken
in this regard?
National Competition Policy
*295. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of COMPANY
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Government  are
considering  'promoting competition'
a  serious  policy  issue  as  envisaged
in  the  NCMP  and  other  statements
made from time to time by Government;
and
(b) what policy initiatives Government
have taken to ensure competition in the
market place?
Insurance cover to people over 55
years
*296. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Insurance Regulatory
Development Authority plans to make it
not mandatory for insurers to service
people over 55 years;
(b) whether, general insurance
companies have already been going slow or
even denying health covers for people over
55 years by disincentivising agents who
sell the policies or simply rejecting such
requests;
(c) whether the premium costs for
55 years and above is already 60 per cent
higher than what a 30 year old has to pay;
and
(d) if so, whether the senior citizens
will be totally deprived of healthcare cover?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

92
Tax Return Preparer Scheme
*297. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA:
SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have entered into arrangement with certain
private organisations who will provide
training to unemployed/underemployed
Graduates to make them as Tax Return
Preparers;
(b) if so, the salient details of the said
agreement entered with the private
organisations, including the total cost of
training to be paid to them, and the salient
features of the proposed training scheme; and
(c) the details of the procedure followed
and exercises made by Government in
selecting these private organisations for the
purpose of rendering training and entering
agreement with them?
Bill to regulate UCB Sector
*298. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to bring
a Bill to regulate and remove the anomalies
in the Urban Co-operative Bank (UCB)
Sector;
(b) if so, the salient features thereof and
by when the Bill would be brought in the
Parliament;
(c) whether Government are aware that
RBI has put on hold scheduling of UCBs,
issue of licenses for new branches etc. in
view of the proposed Bill;
(d) whether Government would direct
RBI to issue licenses to UCBs to open
new branches;
(e) if so, the number of applications by
UCBs for new branches pending with RBI;
and
(f) by when, they would be given
permission?
Opening of regional centre of Sahitya
Academy in Patna
†*299. SHRI JABIR HUSAIN: Will the
Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that at present
four regional centres of Sahitya Academy
are functional in Bangalore, Chennai,
Mumbai and Kolkata in the country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that no regional
centre of the academy has so far been opened
in Hindi-Urdu speaking areas; and
(c) if so, by when Government will take
the necessary decision on opening a regional
centre of Sahitya Academy in Patna (Bihar)
while considering the demand?
Supply of gas to co-operative societies
*300. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of localities where piped
cooking gas connections have been given in
each of the Metro cities in the country;
(b) whether it is a fact that preference
in this regard is given to areas where co-
operative societies are located; and
(c) if so, the details of such areas in the
aforesaid Metro cities not yet covered along
with the reasons therefor?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 6th December, 2006 Secretary-General.

Facilities to physically challenged
passengers
2104. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that DGCA has
asked domestic airlines to be sensitive to
the needs of physically challenged
following a litany of complaints from
passengers;
(b) if so, the details of the directions
issued in this regard;
(c) whether the directions have been
implemented; if so, to what extent; and
(d) if not, the reasons for non-
implementation?
Land for development of airports
†2105. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the names of airports for which land
has been given to Airports Authority of
India for development by the State
Government of Madhya Pradesh;
(b) whether the work on these airports
have been completed; and
(c) if not, the reasons for non-
completion of work and by when the work
is likely to be completed?
Improvement in baggage screening at
airport
2106. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have received proposals from various
quarters for better baggage screening at
airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that India is
one of the few countries where passengers
baggage-to-be checked is subject to pre-
screening before being presented at the
airlines check-in counter?
Revival of closed airports
2107. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be

(a) the details of the airports in the
country closed during the last few years;

the reasons therefor?
US assistance in civil aviation sector
2108. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Federal Aviation
Authority of the United States and the
Ministry signed a Memorandum of
Agreement paving the way for technical
assistance from US on a host of aviation
related matters;
(b) if so, what are the other main
features of the agreement;

(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute

Government are planning to simplify the
licence of pilots under new training system;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be

building the infrastructure of the country

Delay in AI-188 flight

BAJWA: Will the Minister of CIVIL

(a) whether a broken pipe was found in
the toilet of aircraft on AI-188 flight which
took off from Toronto airport on the 18th
September, 2006 and had to return to
Toronto after an hour flight as a result
thereof;
(b) if so, whether the incident has been
probed; and
(c) if so, the findings thereof and  the
action taken thereon?
Promotion of regional airlines
2112. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that to promote

to exempt their carriers from paying airport
and navigation charges in the first five years
of operation;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government are also contemplating to
extend subsidy to airlines on bidding basis

the North East and Jammu and Kashmir;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
New airport at Ludhiana
2113. SHRI TARLOCHAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be

(a) whether Government have given the

(b) if so, the details of the project; and
(c) whether this new project will affect
the working of airport at Amritsar?
Operation of Pune airport
2114. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: Will the

civilian airport at Pune and by when it
would be operational?
Introduction of airbus service in
North East
2115. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian
Airlines cannot maintain its schedule for
want of sufficient number of aircrafts and
pilots;
(b) what steps are being taken to
overcome this problem;
(c) whether the services of airbuses will
be increased in the North East; and
(d) if so, the details of  the programme?
Relaxation in carrying of liquid
products by passengers

the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the date when the restriction was
imposed regarding carrying liquid products
by the passengers in the planes and the
reasons therefor;
(b) whether Government are considering
to give relaxation in this regard;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the arrangements being made to see
that there is no misuse of the relaxation
given by Government regarding carrying
the liquid products?
Development of airports in Tamil
Nadu

the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be

being made for the development of
Coimbatore, Madurai and Trichi airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government have taken a decision to
commence the work on modernisation of
Chennai airport; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Shortage of flight instructors
†2118. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) what efforts are being made to meet
shortage of pilots and flight instructors;
(b) whether facilities regarding their
training would be enhanced;
(c) whether assistance from other flying
clubs would also be sought for their training
apart from the Indira Gandhi National
Flying Academy; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Pilot training school at Gondia
†2119. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in view of
acute shortage of pilots in the country, a
decision has been taken to set up a state-
of-art pilot training school in Gondia district
of Vidarbha;
(b) if so, whether collaboration have
been made with any foreign company
therein;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) by when this training school would
be completed?
New airport at Karwar
2120. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up an airport at Karwar in Karnataka;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether other airports  in Karnataka,
particularly, Mangalore airport, is upgraded
to facilitate operation of more high capacity
international flights; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Refering of IA to BIFR
2121. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Airlines is going to
be referred to BIFR;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether the profit earned by Indian
Airlines for the last three financial years
has been taken into consideration before
referring the company to BIFR?
Financial performance of Alliance Air/
I.A.

CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the details of profit earned by Indian
Airlines during 1993-94, 1994-95 and
1995-96, year-wise;
(b) whether Alliance Air, subsidiary of
Indian Airlines submits separate balance
sheet;
(c) if so, how much profit has been
earned by Alliance Air during 1993-94,
1994-95 and 1995-96, year-wise; and
(d) whether there is any bearing upon
profit and loss of Indian Airlines on account
of profit and loss of Alliance Air?
Guidelines for operation of small
aircrafts
2123. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

484
(a) whether Government have
formulated Route Disposal Guidelines for
operating small aircrafts/helicopters in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government would
introduce helicopter service between places
of tourists/pilgrims interest in the country?
Naming of Jaipur airport
†2124. SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether a proposal to name the
international airport at Jaipur after Maharaja
Sawai Mansingh is under consideration; and
(b) if so, by when it is proposed to be
done?
New Scanner Machine at Delhi
Airport
†2125. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a machine
installed at Delhi Airport can scan even the
inner wears of the human being;
(b) whether it will not amount to
violation of privacy; and
(c) whether air passengers are regularly
informed of the fact that they can be seen
naked through the machine?
Air service between Delhi and Goa
2126. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Indian Airlines have
stopped running a direct flight from Goa to
Delhi;
(b) if so, the reasons for the premier
national airline to neglect one of the most
internationally favoured tourist destination;
and
(c) whether the Indian Airlines propose
to restart the service in near future?
Change in time of Delhi-
Bhubaneswar flight
2127. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA : Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the occupancy rate in the Indian
Airlines flights from Bhubaneswar to Delhi
and Delhi to Bhubaneswar during the last
one year;
(b) the reasons for which the convenient
time in the morning and the evening are not
being considered inspite of repeated
demands;
(c) the numbers and names of State
capitals which face similar inconvenience/
discrimination as Bhubaneswar in respect
of flight timing; and
(d) whether the Indian Airlines now
consider changing the timings to enable
passengers to get back to Delhi/

that other airlines have started competing
on the same route?
New applications for operation of
scheduled airlines
2128. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
formulate set of guidelines which will make
it mandatory for new and existing
companies to disclose funding for aircrafts
they plan to acquire/on lease;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

485
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that some airlines
are not operating on sound financials and
showing losses; and
(d) what are the total number of
applications pending as on 31st October,
2006 for more than six months seeking
approval for schedule airlines license with
the reasons for delay?
Completion of Bangalore
International Airport Project
2129. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the work of implementation
of Bangalore International Airport Project
is progressing satisfactorily;
(b) if so, the details regarding the
progress work of the runway, terminal
building, construction of Air Traffic Control
Tower, Communication system, IT system,
safety and security system etc.;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) what is the target set-up for
completion of the work and functioning of
the airport?
Delays in service of private airline
operators
2130. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Private
Airline Operators specially Air-Deccan
flights get delayed very frequently
throughout the country;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor alongwith
the details thereof, operator-wise; and
(c) what is the action being taken to
curtail the delays?
Fund for security of airports
2131. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to spend Rs.
160 crore on surveillance at airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the action plan of
Government to beef-up security at airports
across the Country in the wake of Mumbai
bomb blasts?
National Competition Policy
2132. DR. PRABHA THAKUR : Will
the Minister of COMPANY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is as yet no broader
policy framework underlining the role of
competition in the reform process even
though the country is following a policy of
market oriented economic reforms for the
past one and a half decade;
(b) whether Government are considering
adoption of a National Competition Policy
for ensuring consistency and coherence
across various Government policies on the
touchstone of competition; and
(c) if so, what measures have been taken
in this direction?
Slow process of winding up of
companies
2133. SHRI JAI PARKASH
